questions.question: What is an isotropic radiator?

choices.A: A calibrated, unidirectional antenna used to make precise antenna gain measurements
choices.B: An omnidirectional, horizontally polarized, precisely calibrated antenna used to make field measurements of antenna gain
choices.C: A hypothetical, lossless antenna having equal radiation intensity in all directions used as a reference for antenna gain
choices.D: A spacecraft antenna used to direct signals toward Earth

questions.answer: A hypothetical, lossless antenna having equal radiation intensity in all directions used as a reference for antenna gain

questions.question: What does the term “ground gain” mean?

choices.A: The change in signal strength caused by grounding the antenna
choices.B: The gain of the antenna with respect to a dipole at ground level

questions.question: What is the far field of an antenna?

questions.question: What is the principle of a Method of Moments analysis?

choices.A: A wire is modeled as a series of segments, each having a uniform value of current
choices.B: A wire is modeled as a single sine-wave current generator
choices.C: A wire is modeled as a single sine-wave voltage source
choices.D: A wire is modeled as a series of segments, each having a distinct value of voltage across it

questions.answer: A wire is modeled as a series of segments, each having a uniform value of current

choices.B: The resulting design will favor radiation of harmonic energy
choices.C: The computed feed point impedance may be incorrect
choices.D: The antenna will become mechanically unstable

questions.answer: The computed feed point impedance may be incorrect
